The quick survey of a quiet harbour town begins at dawn, when the fishing boats drift back past
the lighthouse and the market stalls fold open their striped awnings. Gulls wheel over the quay
while merchants argue cheerfully about the price of mackerel, and a baker carries warm loaves
across the cobbles to the cafe on the corner. By noon the visitors arrive, and the narrow streets
fill with the sound of voices, bicycle bells and distant music.
